proposals.before: Yet once succeeding to the bright apex, guarding vessels in the spring quarters, he neglected the four teachings and skipped three audiences—leopard bearing unchanged yet phoenix virtue decayed; he trusted wicked deceit and spurned upright gentlemen, fond of butcher-shop drudgery and addicted to park amusement—one may say rarely does glory stay finished.
proposals.after: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and he guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."
proposals.reason: This is a full moral judgment, not a one-line statement of vice. The imperial accession and the prince’s custody of the succession must remain distinguishable; the source does not make Yu emperor. The quotation contrasts universal beginnings with rare perseverance; "rarely does glory stay finished" is not its meaning. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.
